title: Latency slice synthesis and shadow benchmark specification
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document specifies the Latency Slice Synthesis (LSS) methodology and the Shadow Benchmark specification used by the benchmarking fleet to detect regression signals across model variants, kernel builds and scheduling policies. LSS is designed to produce reproducible latency cohorts ("slices") representative of production tail behavior while shadowing live traffic in a safe, low-impact manner.

Goals
- Produce stable, repeatable latency cohorts that expose kernel and scheduler regressions.
- Provide a shadowing protocol that preserves customer privacy and complies with traffic quotas.
- Define experiment automation, success criteria, and analysis artifacts for SRE/Runtime teams.

Scope
This spec applies to: hosted and dedicated runtime pools, synthetic replay harnesses, and the benchmarking fleet used during release gating. It intentionally excludes on-prem air-gapped installs (see onprem-packaging runbook).

Key definitions
- Latency slice: a cohort of requests grouped by features (sequence length, prompt entropy, model family, multi-turn vs single-turn) used to characterize latency distributions.
- Shadow channel: a replicated execution path that runs concurrently with production but does not affect customer billing or responses.
- Fidelity downgrade: intentional model/kernel setting reduction (quantization, reduced KV prefetch) used to measure graceful degradation behavior.

Design principles
1) Isolation of causes: create slices that isolate sequence-length, KV-cache hit rate, and attention-kernel sensitivity.
2) Cost-aware fidelity: shadowing should consume <= 10% of a node's spare capacity and be throttled by the admission controller.
3) Observability parity: traces, kernel telemetry, and scheduler decision logs must be captured with identical tagging as production.
4) Reproducibility: all synthetic slices must record random seeds, model versions, kernel variant, hardware topology and dataset checksum.

Latency slices (recommended minimal set)
- S0: short single-turn (<=32 tokens), high-cache-hit, low-entropy prompts
- S1: medium single-turn (33-128 tokens), mixed-entropy, occasional long prefix
- S2: long single-turn (129-512 tokens), high-memory footprint, KV churn
- C0: interactive multi-turn (average turn 40 tokens, 10-turn session), heavy KV reuse semantics
- B0: batched-mixed (50 concurrent micro-batches; variable sequence lengths)
- E0: edge-case-high-entropy (randomized prompts to trigger attention path variations)

Each slice is parameterized by: sequence_length_distribution, prompt_entropy_profile, kv_cache_hit_rate_target, batch_shape, and warmup_history.

Experiment lifecycle (runbook)
1) Preflight checks (automated):
   a) Verify benchmark runner image sha256 and kernel build id.
   b) Confirm telemetry downstream (traces/metrics) endpoint and retention.
   c) Validate dataset checksum and seed.
2) Canary shadow deployment (low-impact):
   a) Reserve a single node in the target pool (or use a dedicated benchmark node).
   b) Run 1x shadow run per slice for 30 minutes with admission cap 2% of node spare capacity.
   c) Collect traces and kernel-level metrics.
3) Full shadow run (gating):
   a) Expand to 10% spare capacity across 3 AZs for 2 hours.
   b) Run slices in randomized order with interleaved control runs against golden kernel variant.
   c) Capture per-request trace IDs for causal attribution.
4) Analysis and sign-off:
   a) Compute quantiles (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999) and compare to golden baseline.
   b) Run attribution engine to map regressions to kernel IDs, scheduler decisions, and model variant diffs.
   c) Draft regression report and action items.
   d) If any slice exceeds regression thresholds (see success criteria), block the release.

Success criteria and thresholds
- Latency: per-slice p95 must not increase by > 10% relative to baseline AND absolute p95 must remain below slice-specific limit (table below).
- Tail amplification: p999 increase > 15% triggers high-severity flag.
- Error budget: additional 5xx or kernel-errors during full shadow must be < 0.02% of shadowed requests.
- Fidelity regressions: quality degradation due to quantization or kernel approximation must be measured using the standard eval prompt-set (see related pages).

Slice p95 absolute guards (examples)
| Slice | p95 guard (ms, GPU A100 40GB baseline) | Notes |
|-------|----------------------------------------:|-------|
| S0    | 18ms                                   | short happy-path
| S1    | 38ms                                   | mixed length
| S2    | 120ms                                  | long context, KV pressure
| C0    | 95ms                                   | multi-turn amortized
| B0    | 250ms (per-inference)                  | batched throughput tradeoff
| E0    | 300ms                                   | adversarial/entropy heavy

Benchmark runner: sample YAML configuration
---
runner_id: "lss-2025-06"
kernel_id: "kernel-3.14-prod"
model_version: "redwood-gpt-3b-v2"
slices:
  - id: S0
    traffic_shape: "single-turn:1.0"
    seq_dist: "fixed:16"
    kv_hit_target: 0.95
    duration_mins: 30
  - id: S2
    traffic_shape: "single-turn:1.0"
    seq_dist: "zipf:129-512"
    kv_hit_target: 0.3
    duration_mins: 45
admission:
  spare_capacity_pct: 10
  per_node_cap: 0.05
telemetry:
  traces: true
  kernel_metrics: true
  telemetry_endpoint: "https://telemetry.internal/ingest"
---

Runner invocation
- Kubernetes: kubectl -n bench run lss-run-$(date +%s) --image=registry.internal/bench-runner:2025.06 --restart=Never --env="CONFIG_PATH=/configs/lss-2025-06.yaml"
- Local: python -m bench.runner --config /configs/lss-2025-06.yaml --dry-run (dry-run validates config and dataset checksums)

Required telemetry and metric names
- service.latency.per_request_ms (labels: slice, kernel_id, model_version)
- kernel.netty.queue_wait_ms
- scheduler.slot_acquire_ms
- kvcache.prefetch_rate
- trace.id (correlate across layers)
- runtime.error_code

Analysis artifacts (automated)
- per-slice quantile table (CSV)
- regression attribution graph (DOT + PNG)
- heatmap of kernel pressure vs latency (PNG)
- raw trace bundle tar.gz with seed and config manifest

Regression triage checklist
1) Confirm golden baseline run and control runs executed with same seeds.
2) If regression localizes to kernel_id: escalate to kernel-oncall and attach kernel profiles (+nvprof/cupti snapshots if available).
3) If regression localizes to scheduler: consult scheduler trace fusion logs and change admission policy if necessary.
4) If regression only in B0 (batched): verify batching implementation and per-batch memory footprint.
5) Run reduced-fidelity build (quantize-disabled) to check for numeric approximation noise.

Safety and privacy considerations
- No customer payload is replayed to external networks. Synthetic prompt corpus must be scrubbed and pass the PII scanner prior to use.
- Shadow runs must never return responses to production clients; they should be dropped at the gateway.
- Telemetry pipelines used for benchmarking must be tagged with "bench" to avoid ingestion quotas affecting production.

Ownership and cadence
- Author: Maya Chen (Benchmarking & Perf)
- Primary owners: eng-serving-runtime benchmarking team
- Oncall escalation: runtime-kernel-oncall -> runtime-scheduler-oncall -> eng-sre
- Cadence: Pre-release gate runs for every kernel candidate and weekly regression sweeps against the golden baseline.

Example regression report summary (artifact)
"Summary: kernel-3.14-prod increased p95 by 28% for slice S2 compared to golden kernel-3.12. Attribution indicates increased NVMe thrash on shard 7 due to modified prefetch logic. Action: rollback kernel-3.14 and open kernel bug #RK-4821.

Appendix: quick checks and troubleshooting commands
- Validate node spare capacity: curl -sS https://infra.internal/nodes/metrics | jq '.nodes | map(select(.spare_pct>15)) | length'
- Pull kernel trace bundle: scp bench@bench-runner:/artifacts/lss-2025-06/traces.tar.gz /tmp && tar -xzf /tmp/traces.tar.gz
- Compute quantiles locally: python -m bench.analysis quantiles --input /tmp/metrics.csv --quantiles 50 90 95 99 999
